title: Fake Plastic Trees
feel: Quiet acoustic strum building to full band; slow, about 74 bpm (estimate)

alt_voicings.label: Simpler chart
alt_voicings.note: plain F♯m, D and Bm for the colour chords — a fallback, not the goal

sections.name: Section A (the verse)
sections.bars: A | % | % | Asus4 A | Dmaj9/F# | % | % | E | Dsus2 | A | Dsus2 | %
sections.note: Dmaj9/F♯ is the tab's “A/F♯”; the simple chart plays F♯m there.

sections.name: Section B (the turn)
sections.note: ×2 to ×4 by ear, ending A – Asus4 – A. The bridge is these two bars ×3.

why: Slow, forgiving, and built on one idea: **one 2nd-fret grip held while the bass moves under it** — open A, then the thumb's F♯, then the index's B — with sus4 and sus2 colours one finger away. Every new move is small; the tempo gives you time to make it.
hard_change: **A → Dmaj9/F♯.** Finger A index–middle–ring; keep middle and ring on strings 3–2, lift the index, wrap the thumb over to string 6 fret 2 (its tip mutes string 5). Thumb first, then strum.
theory: I–vi–V–IV in A (A, F♯, E, D); Bm7(add11) is ii. Dmaj9/F♯ stands in for F♯m; the colour voicings keep E and A ringing on top as pedal tones.
steps: The grip alone: A → Dmaj9/F♯ → A → Bm7(add11) → A, the middle finger never leaving string 3.
Section A at about 52 (70%), four slow down-strums a bar; then section B.
A and B in the record's order at 60–67, then with the record: the band gets louder, your part stays the same.
caveat: Tabs label this song's sections differently; “Section A” and “Section B” here are a reconciliation, and the harmony agrees across sources (only the chord names differ). Voicings vary between transcriptions — trust your ear and your teacher's version.
